stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on June 29th.
stocks.news:
Stocks bounced back nicely. The S&P 500 climbed 1.18% to 7,440, the NASDAQ jumped 2.07% to 25,820, and the DOW added 0.59% to 52,182 (figures as of the June 29th close).

The day belonged to the space race. Rocket Lab (RKLB +15.86%) is buying satellite operator Iridium (IRDM +25.44%) for $8 billion, picking up 2.5 million subscribers and a real shot at rivaling Elon Musk's Starlink. Less cheerful: Microsoft (MSFT -1.18%) is headed for its worst month since 2000, having shed about $570 billion in value in June as investors fret that AI could make its own cash cows obsolete.

economy.note: Stock indexes as of the June 29th close; 10-Year, gold, and Brent as of June 29th (Market Briefs); silver is live spot, June 30th (Fortune).
economy.commentary:
The jobs report is the week's big tell. Traders on the Kalshi betting market put only a 42% chance on June adding more than 125,000 jobs, well short of May's surprising 172,000. A soft number would nudge the Fed toward cutting sooner, which would be welcome news for mortgage rates, even if it signals a cooling economy.

Metals slipped. Gold fell 1.54% to $3,976 and silver eased to about $58.50, while copper held just above $6 a pound. Brent crude dipped 0.70% to $72.64 and the 10-year Treasury yield sat flat at 4.37%. For housing, a cooler read on the economy is a double-edged sword: lower rates would help, but only because growth is slowing.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET, June 29th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto drifted lower again, with Bitcoin off 0.52% to $59,847, Ether down 1.30% to $1,589, and XRP off 0.75% to $1.05 (figures as of the June 29th close).

Strategy (MSTR +12.60%), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, may sell up to $1.25 billion of its stash to raise cash, since its sliding share price makes issuing new stock unappealing. Meanwhile big investors are rotating out of Bitcoin and Ether funds and into XRP and HYPE, chasing newer stories while the two majors keep sliding.

real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage Rates Ease To 6.52% As A Soft Jobs Report Looms; Wall Street Keeps Rolling Up Real Estate Managers; The East Bay Board Slips To 2,901 Active On 217 New And 198 Closed
real_estate.commentary:
The 30-year fixed ticked down to 6.52% and the 15-year held at 6.12%. With this week's jobs report in focus, a soft number could pull rates a little lower, but the lock-in effect keeping resale supply tight is not going anywhere until the gap to owners' existing rates narrows.

Wall Street keeps buying the plumbing of real estate. Private equity firm Bridgepoint agreed to buy Kayne Anderson's real estate arm for $1.4 billion, the latest in a string of deals, with Berkshire having scooped up homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $8 billion a few weeks back, as big firms race to offer clients more ways to invest in property.

On the other side of the ledger, Google co-founder Sergey Brin sold his stake in a fund tied to rent-controlled New York apartments for just six cents on the dollar, a reminder that when the rules cap the rent, they cap the value too.

Locally, the East Bay board slipped to 2,901 active (down 44 from yesterday), with 217 new listings against 198 closings. Oakland again led the board with 44 new on 772 active; Fremont added 28 new on 348 active.

For agents: with the jobs report due, do not over-promise on rates, but a softer print could finally give buyers a reason to move. Lean into the steady supply (2,901 active, 217 new) and price discipline. Well-priced, well-presented homes still sell inside about four weeks, while overpriced listings just sit, so the coaching holds: price to today's market and the sale follows.
